criteria.reasoning: The memo opens with "Gerry Halvorsen died at home on Thursday, August 27, 2026," citing the obituary and the probate notice. That is the correct date of death.

It states "The September 29 visit cannot go ahead as a solicitation. The gallery proposal is not to be presented to Peg or anyone in the family." Ruth may make a condolence visit at which "she raises no gift, proposal, pledge or estate matter and brings no proposal or rendering," and the memo forbids proposing a memorial naming.
Action 1 says "Close proposal PR-2026-044 as 'Closed — donor deceased' (not transferred to Peg or anyone else)."

Action 1 says "Mark record 10388 deceased, date of death 2026-08-27 ... Remove Gerry from all appeals, mailings, e-mail lists and event invitations." Action 2 pulls the household's Fall Appeal row before the 2026-09-28 printer date.
It flags the family "Bereavement — no solicitation before 2027-02-23," which it identifies as "the 180th day after the 2026-08-27 date of death." That is the correct date.

Action 2 says to "Pull the Fall Appeal rows for both the Halvorsen household (10388/10389, Peg) and Kristin and Michael Doyle (20417) before the mail file goes to the printer." Both surviving family rows are removed, not re-addressed.

Action 6 says "Do not send the Halvorsen Family Foundation letter of request due October 15. A request to a foundation whose trustees are Peg, Erik and Kristin is a solicitation, and none may go before 2027-02-23."
It gives "Unpaid balance: $70,000 ($200,000 − $130,000)," explains that the CRM's $80,000 misses the 2026-06-12 $10,000 check, and says the Annual Fund and gala gifts do not reduce the balance.

Action 7 refers the $70,000 to "CFO Denise Okafor" and says "Only Denise decides whether to present a claim and deals with the estate about the pledge. No one in development asks Peg, Erik, Kristin or the family foundation to pay it, and no pledge reminder goes to the household." Section 4 adds that no one is to discuss the pledge with "Erik in his role as personal representative."
The pledge referral includes "personal representative Erik T. Halvorsen (attorney Laura Vang, Vang & Steinke, S.C.), and the claims deadline of 2026-12-28," along with case 2026PR000214.

Action 8 says "Notify Samuel Achterberg of the $100,000 bequest intention. He alone contacts the personal representative or the estate's attorney to learn whether the will includes a gift to the Center."
It says "Keep it as an expectancy: it is not booked as revenue, a receivable or campaign credit until the estate's distribution is received," and notes "A bequest intention is revocable."
Action 5 says the condolence letter "is signed by President & CEO Laurel Whitfield and co-signed by Board Chair Thomas Brandvold" because Gerry was a former trustee.
It notes the three memorial gifts received and the obituary's direction to arts education. Action 9 says to "send Peg a monthly list of memorial donors' names and addresses, never the amounts."

The facts stated (birth date, survivors, service dates, foundation trustees, pledge payments, memorial donors, probate details, letter of intent) all trace to the files. The memo gives no cause of death or estate value and says "We do not know whether the will ... still contains" the bequest. Treating Dale and Joan Halvorsen as not this family is consistent with the obituary's survivor list.
